title: How to Get "That Winning Feeling"
coreMove: Train the winning feeling by recalling real past success, rehearsing favorable outcomes, and giving the automatic mechanism a goal that feels presently possible.

exampleSpecs.audience: Haruto, an amateur golfer trying to recover steadiness before a match
exampleSpecs.stakes: A technical checklist may crowd out the bodily confidence that made prior shots work.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Cary Middlecoff and successful shots to show remembered bodily confidence before action.

exampleSpecs.audience: Aubrey, a lifter meeting a heavy set after a failed attempt
exampleSpecs.stakes: The body may organize around collapse if the mental picture treats the load as already lost.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the weightlifter example connecting load, expectation, and performance.

exampleSpecs.audience: Estelle, a project lead preparing for a difficult client review
exampleSpecs.stakes: Her imagination is rehearsing failure with more force than it gives the desired result.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn ordinary worry into positive worry by rehearsing a favorable outcome and goal picture.

exampleSpecs.audience: Beatriz, a new account manager recovering after a flat call
exampleSpecs.stakes: Abstract encouragement will not steady her as well as a concrete memory of competence.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a past victory and first sale as evidence that the successful state has existed before.

exampleSpecs.audience: Isabella, a speaker waiting behind the curtain
exampleSpecs.stakes: A vague pep talk can inflate anxiety, while a precise memory can restore readiness.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use speech and past victory memory to make confidence accessible before performance.

exampleSpecs.audience: Marlowe, a student rebuilding confidence after a poor practice score
exampleSpecs.stakes: The failed score can become the only rehearsal unless a real success memory is brought back online.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use exam and past victory recall to show small wins as believable confidence material.
